authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8056.1 pāda lists Prakrit pāya, Hindi pā/pā̃u “foot, leg”, Old Marwari pāya/pāva and Marathi/Gujarati pāy. It discusses final u/v as incorporation of inflectional endings, with pādu an explicitly less probable alternative; that qualification is retained. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10203 mudrā gives Prakrit muddā/muddiā “seal, ring”, Oriya mudi, Konkani muddi and Lahnda mundrī. The dental mudi/mundi/mundari forms fit this signet-ring family; retroflex survey variants are kept for a separate consonant review. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10951 lamba gives Prakrit laṃba, Punjabi/Lahnda lammā, Western Pahari lammo, Kumauni lāmo, Gujarati lāmbu and Maithili namā “long”. Thus Magahi namma has a documented eastern n- comparator rather than being rejected as an unexplained spelling. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open.
